what: Has a real project's own check ever been shown able to see a change at the site a lesson would fire at? Measured by generating byte-splice mutants of one file, running the project's own test command on each, and counting the sites where every perturbation was caught by a test that passed before it.

method.mutants: AST-verified single-line byte splices; ROR, AOR, LCR, RVR; a splice is kept only when it still parses and changes the parsed program
method.catch_rule: SWE-bench's fail-to-pass rule at mutant granularity: a mutant is caught when a test that PASSED on the unmutated source did not pass on the mutant. Pre-existing failures are therefore harmless and are not excluded by hand
method.site_licensed: every mutant generated at the site was caught
method.load_probe: the check must fail on an unparseable version of the file, or it does not import the file and nothing is measured
method.budget: max_sites=10, max_mutants=24, sites in line order, no sampling
method.restore: original bytes restored in a finally and verified by hash before the next mutant
method.corpora: codeload.github.com tarballs of the default branch: torproject/stem, more-itertools/more-itertools, pypa/packaging

finding_1_every_file_was_partial.measured: 0 of 5 files were fully licensed; between 1 and 5 sites per file were blind
finding_1_every_file_was_partial.interpretation: A lesson placed at a blind site is blessed by the check without the check being able to disagree. On these five files that is 24% of the places a lesson could land -- a quarter of one-shot lessons would receive a verdict the suite cannot support.

finding_2_the_survivors_are_mostly_boole.measured_example: stem/util/tor_tools.py lines 70, 76, 94, 112 are four `return False` guards in Tor version predicates; replacing the whole return with `None` is still falsy, so no test distinguishes them
finding_2_the_survivors_are_mostly_boole.interpretation: This is a known weakness of whole-return mutation (RVR), not a new fact about the project. It is reported as a refused site and named, so a reader can see the operator, and it is the honest reason the per-file figures are not 100%.

finding_3_quantity_is_not_licence.interpretation: With five files this rank correlation is suggestive and nothing more; it is reported as an ordering, not as a coefficient with a p-value. It is the reason the next measurement is worth making: if it holds at n=50, 'make the check cheap to stand up' and 'make the check able to see the change' are the same work, and the repository's #1 bottleneck has a measurable proxy.

finding_4_cost.what_drives_it: the size of the check's own run: 145 passing tests cost 25 s per mutant, 2 passing tests cost 0.45 s
finding_4_cost.consequence: A licence must be bought once and reused. It is content-addressed on the file's hash, the check command and the budget, so an unchanged file costs nothing the second time.

finding_5_the_harness_is_the_first_failu.measured: pypa/packaging is src-layout. Without `extra_paths=('src',)`, `import packaging` resolved to the installed copy, the mutant was written to a file nothing opened, and the first run reported 0 of 8 sites licensed -- 'the tests are blind' when the truth was 'the harness measured other code'
finding_5_the_harness_is_the_first_failu.fix: a load probe: an unparseable version of the file must break at least one previously-passing test, or the measurement is REFUSED
finding_5_the_harness_is_the_first_failu.why_it_matters: this is the same class of error as the round-13 finder bug, one layer down

what_this_does_not_say: not a proof that a licensed site is correct -- only that THIS set of perturbations was seen
not a claim that a refused site is a defect in the project's tests
not a benchmark; three repositories, five files, chosen for having runnable suites, not sampled
not a claim that the ordering in finding 3 is causal or significant at n=5
no model was called, no capability registered, no family flipped, truth.achieved is untouched, spend is $0
